title: UNPACKING HUMAN PREFERENCE FOR LLMS: DEMOGRAPHICALLY AWARE EVALUATION WITH THE HUMAINE FRAMEWORK

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing aggregated 'universal' LLM preference leaderboards against demographically adjusted rankings using a hierarchical Bayesian Bradley-Terry-Davidson model post-stratified to census data to expose the blind spots of unrepresentative rater pools.

Analyzing human pairwise preference comparisons of LLMs across distinct age cohorts (18-34, 35-54, 55+) to measure preference heterogeneity, showing that a model's perceived rank shifts substantially based on user age.
Measuring variance in LLM preference rankings by stratifying human evaluators across various ethnic groups in the US and UK to see if preference patterns diverge based on user ethnicity.

Evaluating differences in pairwise LLM preferences by stratifying human evaluators based on their political affiliations (e.g., Democrat vs. Republican, Conservative vs. Labour) and measuring interaction effects with other demographics.
Comparing human preference interactions, tie rates, and demographic interaction effects (e.g., age × politics) between United States and United Kingdom user populations.
